title: arxiv_2006.12943v1
universal_lens: Distributed tracking as a probabilistic state transition system with data-dependent communication bounds. A unified framework for estimating item arrival frequencies in distributed systems using empirical Bernstein bounds and adaptive slack mechanisms to minimize communication overhead while maintaining statistical accuracy.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference framework for dynamic threshold crossing using learned data distributions in GSI's probabilistic tracking models. Bayesian inference models estimate μi using empirical means ̄μi, applying conformal prediction bounds to quantify uncertainty and adjust decision thresholds dynamically across players.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state-machine transitions in GSE for distributed counters, with adaptive algorithms based on observed data patterns. Situational reasoning maps estimated frequencies ̄μi into adaptive slacks, enabling state transitions that balance tracking fidelity with communication efficiency in real-time distributed environments.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter window 3 focuses on refining empirical estimates of item arrival rates in distributed systems to enable efficient communication protocols. The core idea begins with learning an unknown distribution through the CMY algorithm during a first round, which yields estimates ̄μi for each player's arrival rate. These estimates are inherently noisy and potentially biased, especially when sample sizes are limited. To address this, the paper introduces the Empirical Bernstein Bound to quantify estimation error and derive upper confidence bounds UBi for the number of items ni that will arrive at each player. However, direct substitution of ̄μi into these bounds may lead to overly optimistic (and thus unsafe) upper limits. Therefore, a correction step constructs ˆμi ≥ μi to guarantee validity of UBi. Finally, adjustments to the threshold t ensure that the sum of all UBi does not exceed the total communication budget N. This process enables a principled trade-off between tracking accuracy and communication efficiency, forming the basis for adaptive slack mechanisms in GSE.
